GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.
 The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.
 * Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab. 
 An overview of this role 
 As a Staff Corporate Security Engineer, you'll help secure the systems GitLab team members rely on every day across a fully remote environment. This role sits within Corporate Security Engineering and focuses on building secure-by-default controls for endpoints and the SaaS platforms that support them, with a strong emphasis on macOS. You'll own meaningful technical decisions around endpoint hardening, automation, and detection, and you'll help turn security requirements into scalable engineering systems that are measurable, auditable, and designed to reduce friction for end users.
 This is a strong fit if you're motivated by solving security problems with code. You will work across endpoint management, identity, and security operations to improve how GitLab manages macOS, iOS, Windows, and Linux devices through Infrastructure-as-Code, Terraform, and GitOps workflows. In your first year, you'll be expected to strengthen endpoint security architecture, expand automation, and improve the reliability and auditability of how controls are deployed and maintained.
 What you’ll do 
 Lead the security architecture of GitLab's endpoint fleet and related infrastructure, with a primary focus on macOS.
 Design and support automation for secure endpoint deployment, configuration, and lifecycle management using code-based workflows.
 Manage endpoint and SaaS security configuration through Terraform, version control, merge requests, continuous integration pipelines, and automated rollouts.
 Define and enforce security baselines across macOS, iOS, Windows, and Linux endpoints.
 Develop patching and software distribution approaches that align with security, compliance, and operational requirements.
 Partner with Information Technology, Security Operations, and Detection and Response teams to improve endpoint telemetry, detections, and response models.
 Drive process improvements that reduce manual work and lower risk by favoring automation, policy-driven controls, and auditable change management.
 Mentor engineers across Corporate Security and Information Technology, and serve as a senior escalation point for complex endpoint security issues.
 What you’ll bring 
 Experience designing and delivering endpoint, systems, or corporate security solutions in environments that require scalable, durable controls.
 Deep knowledge of endpoint management platforms such as Jamf Pro or FleetDM, especially for architecting and securing macOS environments.
 Strong hands-on ability with Terraform and Infrastructure-as-Code practices, including module design, state management, and pipeline-based deployment.
 Experience working with GitOps workflows where changes are managed through Git repositories, merge requests, code review, and automated pipelines.
 Strong proficiency in scripting or programming for automation and security tooling, such as bash, Python, PowerShell, or Go.
 Familiarity with cloud identity providers and directories, including platforms such as Okta, Google Workspace, LDAP.
 Ability to communicate clearly, collaborate across distributed teams, and work independently in an all-remote environment.
 Openness to bringing transferable experience from adjacent security, systems, or platform engineering backgrounds, along with a practical and security-focused approach to problem solving.
 About the team 
 The Corporate Security Engineering team secures the internal environment GitLab team members use every day, including endpoints, identity systems, SaaS applications, and platforms that store sensitive internal data. It's a small, high-leverage team that treats security work as engineering work: building with code, operating through Git, and using reviewable, testable, and auditable workflows by default. The team partners closely with Information Technology, Security Operations, and Engineering across regions, collaborating asynchronously to build controls that scale across GitLab's all-remote workforce while reducing friction for end users.

HELLO!

I’m Allie, Head of Support at Ashby. 👋 Knowledge is one of the most important levers we have for delivering a great customer experience. Our knowledge ecosystem shapes how customers learn Ashby, how our Specialists resolve tickets, and how many customers never need to file a ticket at all. We have a tenured, talented Knowledge Management team doing excellent work. What we’re missing is someone to unify its work into a single, strategic practice.

That’s why we’re hiring our first Director of Knowledge Management. You’ll lead a team of Knowledge Managers and expand the team into new areas, including Digital Support experience and content localization.

You’ll set the vision, standards, and operating model that connect our customer-facing Help Center, internal Knowledge Base, and the self-service and in-app experiences built on them, including our AI Assistant. You’ll coach and develop a team that is growing and taking on new kinds of work, and you’ll be the voice of Knowledge in conversations with Support, Customer Success, Product, Engineering, and beyond.

 


ABOUT THE ROLE

Today, our Knowledge Managers divide their work between internal and external content. You’ll help the team decide where to focus next, in what order, and how its structure should evolve to deliver on those priorities.

Knowledge Management is its own function at Ashby, separate from the internal and external enablement teams. You’ll build strong partnerships with both, defining clear boundaries and handoffs so content is consistent, never duplicated, and never left without an owner.

Your team will also co-own the AI Assistant’s self-service experience with Product, helping customers find the right knowledge when and where they need it. You’ll stay close enough to the content to coach with specifics, while relying on your team for the day-to-day execution of knowledge governance.




WHAT YOU’LL OWN:

Set the Direction for Knowledge

 - Define the vision, roadmap, and success measures for Knowledge Management across internal and external content.

 - Identify the highest-impact opportunities to improve the knowledge ecosystem and sequence them against team capacity.

 - Build a clear model for content ownership, governance, and quality, streamlining how content is created, reviewed, and kept current as our product evolves.

 - Champion Knowledge-Centered Service (KCS) practices and drive adoption across Support.

Lead and Develop the Team

 - Coach and develop Knowledge Managers through specific feedback on their work, clear career paths, and growth opportunities.

 - Evolve the team’s structure and divide work in the way that best serves customers and the business, with room to move beyond the current internal/external split.

 - Hire and onboard new team members next year, including Knowledge Managers, a Digital Support experience role, and a localization role.

Shape the AI Assistant’s Self-Service Experience

 - Co-own the AI Assistant’s self-service experience with Product, aligning on strategy, roadmap, and quality and partnering with Support, Support Operations, and Engineering on design and testing.

 - Help lead both declarative flows (structured, designed paths) and generative flows (AI-composed answers grounded in our content), and decide when each is the right tool.

 - Shape how content is structured, tagged, and governed so the Assistant surfaces accurate, current answers.

Build Our Localization Strategy

 - Build our localization strategy for Help Center content and drive the translation strategy for Customer Education, balancing quality, speed, and cost.

 - Define priorities for languages, content types, and tooling, and put processes in place to keep translated content in sync with the source.

Measure and Improve Results

 - Define and report on knowledge health, including content usage, search success, deflection, article quality, freshness, and the impact of knowledge on ticket volume and handle time. Treat deflection as a signal of customer success, not just cost reduction.

 - Measure how well the AI Assistant resolves customer questions, and use those conversations, ticket trends, customer feedback, and Specialist input to identify gaps and set content priorities.

Partner Across Ashby

 - Work closely with Customer Education and internal enablement in RevOps to align on ownership, standards, and a shared view of the customer and employee learning journey.

 - Partner with Product Marketing and Engineering so documentation keeps pace with releases and launches.




REQUIREMENTS

 - Multiple years of experience leading knowledge management or content programs, setting strategy and building processes that scale with the business, ideally in B2B SaaS Support or Customer Experience.

 - Experience managing a team of content or knowledge professionals, including coaching people at different levels of experience.

 - Ability to connect knowledge across internal and external audiences, aligning Support, Product, Marketing, Engineering, and enablement teams around clear ownership and shared standards.

 - Experience designing or operating self-service or AI-assisted support experiences, including both structured and generative flows, and a point of view on how knowledge quality shapes their performance.

 - Experience defining success measures for knowledge and using data to prioritize and make tradeoffs.

 - Comfort working in ambiguity as the function’s first dedicated leader, building on existing practices while setting a clear direction.

 - Strong writing and editing instincts. You’ll stay close enough to the work to set a high quality bar and give specific feedback.

 - Experience with KCS or comparable methodologies.




YOU SHOULD APPLY IF:

 - You’ve led a knowledge management, documentation, or content program and managed a team of knowledge or content professionals.

 - You’ve designed or operated self-service or AI-assisted support experiences, including structured and generative flows, and understand how knowledge quality affects their performance.

 - You’re a strong writer and editor who can give specific feedback on the work, coach people at different levels, and help them grow.

 - You see knowledge as a strategic lever for customer experience and can bring teams together around clear ownership, shared standards, and measurable results.

 - You’re excited to build on an experienced team, shape how the function operates, and expand into new areas like Digital Support experience and localization.

 


YOU SHOULD NOT APPLY IF:

 - Your background doesn’t include both managing a knowledge or content team and setting strategy for a knowledge, documentation, or content program.

 - You haven’t designed or operated self-service or AI-assisted support experiences.

 - You want a purely strategic role that keeps you removed from the content and the detailed feedback your team needs.

 - You need a fully built, fully staffed function or an established playbook to step into. We have a strong foundation, but several roles are still to be hired and the operating model is still taking shape.

 - You want sole ownership of AI product decisions or prefer to work only within a team you manage. This role depends on shared decisions with Product and strong partnerships across Ashby.

 


ABOUT ASHBY

Ashby builds a suite of products that helps talent leaders, recruiters, and hiring managers run their hiring process significantly better. We raised a $50M Series D in July 2025 and support nearly 5,000 customers, including Shopify, Snowflake, OpenAI, Deliveroo, and Confluent. We’re growing much faster than 100% year over year, with a team of roughly 300 people across 22+ countries. Learn more at ashbyhq.com http://ashbyhq.com.

 


ABOUT GO TO MARKET

We view our Support team as an extension of the product itself, one that ensures an optimal customer experience for customers ranging across all market segments. Here are a few points that should give you an idea of what it is like to work with us:

 - We spend a lot of time building best-in-class products since we believe a highly differentiated product is easier to sell.

 - We also spend a lot of time building a best-in-class customer experience. We aim to offer deep expertise whenever we interact with prospects and customers.

 - We strongly believe that small teams with very talented people and the right work environment deliver much better performance than teams with large headcount.

We value a strong sense of ownership, principled thinking over experience, and thoughtful communication (we put a lot of effort into using the right communication channels) - we’ll get into these and other values during the hiring process.  - 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby—do it when you feel financially comfortable.

 - Twelve weeks of fully paid family leave in the US. We plan to expand this to employees in other countries as situations arise.

 - A $1,200 annual learning and professional-development budget.

 - A one-time $2,000 home-office setup budget for furniture, monitors, peripherals, and ergonomic equipment, plus a company-provided laptop.

Secure Every Identity, from AI to Human
 Identity is the key to unlocking the potential of AI. Okta secures AI by building the trusted, neutral infrastructure that enables organizations to safely embrace this new era. This work requires a relentless drive to solve complex challenges with real-world stakes. We are looking for builders and owners who operate with speed and urgency and execute with excellence.
This is an opportunity to do career-defining work. We're all in on this mission. If you are too, let's talk.
 The Agent Gateway Team
 The Agent Gateway team owns the identity-aware infrastructure that connects enterprise AI agents to the tools, data, and services their organizations authorize. Every call from Claude, Agentforce, Codex, and internal/homegrown agents to a resource flows through us. We enforce authorization, isolate credentials, mint the right token per target, and produce the audit trails that security teams rely on.
 We are early in a rapidly evolving space. The standards for agent identity (MCP, OAuth token exchange, DCR) are being built under our feet. Our roadmap includes hardening the data plane for on-premises customer deployments, extending policy semantics beyond tool-level allowlists, adding native support for Agent-to-Agent brokered delegation, and scaling to tenants with thousands of virtual MCP servers.
 The Senior Software Engineer Opportunity
 Okta is looking for a Senior Software Engineer to help build the Agent Gateway. You will own features and components across the data and control planes, turning technical designs and product requirements into reliable production systems. Working alongside staff engineers, you will implement token exchange, request routing, credential resolution, and policy evaluation as agent identity specifications evolve.
 This is a hands-on software development role at the intersection of product, security, and infrastructure. You will ship services that handle agentic traffic reliably and performantly at scale.
 What You'll Be Doing
 Build and Ship: Own the implementation of gateway features end-to-end — from virtual MCP server aggregation to token exchange and policy evaluation — with tests, observability, and operational readiness built in.
 Work in the Runtime Path: Write code that handles credentials, tokens, tenant isolation, and audit logging with care. The gateway sits in the critical path for customer agent traffic, so correctness and reliability matter on every change.
 Implement the Protocols: Read and implement MCP, OAuth token exchange, and agent identity specifications, and feed production lessons back into designs and reference implementations.
 Ship With Agentic Tooling: Use Claude, Claude Code, and MCP-connected agents as everyday parts of your workflow across design, code generation, code review, and operations.
 Contribute to Quality: Participate in code review, testing, incident response, and our design-doc culture, and help raise the team's engineering bar.
 What You'll Bring to the Role
 Experience: 4+ years building production backend systems, ideally distributed and highly available.
 Technical Depth: Proficiency shipping production services in Java and/or Go.
 Domain Knowledge: Working knowledge of OAuth 2.0 and OIDC, and comfort reading and implementing spec-driven code. Familiarity with RFC 8693 token exchange is a plus.
 Operational Sense: Hands-on experience with service rollouts, feature flags, observability, and incident response.
 Agentic Fluency: Working familiarity with agentic development tools (e.g., Claude Code, MCP servers, AI-assisted code review), with a point of view on where they accelerate work.
 Communication: Clear written and verbal communication, and the ability to collaborate across a data plane service and a larger identity control plane.
 Extra Credit
 Experience building or integrating with an MCP server, an agent framework, or an LLM-facing gateway.
 Prior work on multi-tenant SaaS platforms.
 Exposure to identity, authorization, or edge-of-network services.
 Active participation in standards work in the agent identity space (MCP, OAuth, GNAP, DCR).
 Full-stack or frontend experience for the gateway's admin and configuration surfaces.

 Better Everyday : review every brand moment against its goal, and make the next one bigger, cheaper or better.

You’ll become the internal owner who extends it, keeps it reliable, and drives adoption across Demand Generation and adjacent marketing teams.

You’ll partner with marketers across campaign strategy, lifecycle, paid acquisition, SEO, GEO/AEO, content, CRO, marketing operations, and analytics. You will be surfacing opportunities we can’t currently see and taking on work that simply isn’t practical by hand, like analyzing every creative we’ve run to learn what truly drives performance.  - Own the handover and the foundation
   
   - Take ownership of the assets built during our external engagement: tools, agents, MCP servers, prompts, evals, and documentation, and make sure they remain reliable, understood, and extensible after the vendor rolls off.
   
   - Own and advance the AI maturity model already in motion, moving marketers from first useful wins to regular integration to self-sufficiency, and reporting progress to leadership.
   
   - Own the marketing AI roadmap: prioritize what to build next, decide what to sunset, and set the standards and patterns the team builds against.

 - Build
   
   - Build AI-powered tools, agents, automations, and skills tailored to real marketing workflows - e.g. campaign planning, audience research, content development, channel execution, reporting, experimentation, and optimization.
   
   - Build and maintain integrations that connect AI to live data - e.g., MCP servers linking ad platforms, analytics, and CRM. This is so marketers can work against real data in natural language instead of exporting and reconciling by hand.
   
   - Establish quality and reliability practices: evals, regression tests, and human-in-the-loop review so tools can be trusted against real campaigns and real data, and so they don’t silently break when models or platforms change.

 - Expand what’s possible
   
   - Use AI to uncover opportunities the team can’t currently see: patterns across campaigns, audiences, creative, channels, and content that would be impractical to surface by hand.
